rationale: The spelling correction retains readable English and no fork instruction depends on the original sentence.
The variable is renamed consistently in its declaration and use; the demonstrated call and returned value remain unchanged.
The renderer supports the new paragraph and unordered-list form, preserving readable mode names.
The State definition is retained, and the additional entry does not conflict with a closed-set consumer.
Any text editor remains supported and the preview is optional, so the terminal-only contribution path remains available.
Complete request syntax remains in the bundled API guide; the absent background essay is unnecessary to assess this obligation.
The fork tutorial uses send, which remains documented; deprecating the unused alias does not require adaptation.
Retrying at most twice preserves the limit of two additional attempts after the initial request.
The fork runbook names sync-now, which is explicitly unsupported; it needs to name catalog-refresh instead.
The static renderer lacks InteractiveTable and strips its tag, so the fork needs another means to display mode meanings.
The upstream instructions remove support for handwritten terminal edits, conflicting with the required supported terminal-only path.
Directly republishing French-only defaults no longer provides the required English default messages.
Python 3.11 falls below the new supported floor of 3.13 and cannot be upgraded by this sync, requiring fork-specific handling or a decision.
The fork template consumes the removed explanation field, so preserving upstream requires adapting the template or deciding how to satisfy its obligation.
The directly included quickstart now instructs trainees to commit a source example containing an API key, conflicting with the stated training obligation.
The fork guide still promises thirty days, whereas the upstream submission period is seven days; the fork guide needs adaptation.
The interface changes to version 2, but the absent migration and command mapping are needed to determine whether the version-1 fork script remains compatible.
Whether the architecture remains visible depends on Mermaid support, and the renderer capabilities are not supplied.
The deployed Python version is absent, so compatibility with the new 3.12 minimum cannot be established.
The revised schema is absent, preventing assessment of whether the parser can still read status and summary correctly.
The cohort language is absent, so the new Spanish defaults cannot be compared with the fork training requirement.
The education submission terms are absent, so the accuracy of the local thirty-day guide cannot be assessed.
The surrounding example and mode definition are absent, so the changed call cannot be established as a runnable self-contained example.
The retry conditions expand, but the operator guide is absent, so it is unknown whether that guide already describes them accurately.
The about page publishes this upstream file directly without a separate version string, so preserving the update displays the upstream version.
The plugin remains optional and the unchanged core path explicitly runs without plugins.
Failed requests still return an error; the handler ignores the newly added explanatory text.
The change preserves oldest-first ordering, which is the exercise requirement.
ZIP remains available, and the installer does not depend on the added tar.gz option.
The annotated diagram remains supplied in its existing location; the transcript is additive.
Only an optional example time changes; the scheduler retains its separate operator-selected 14:00 UTC configuration.
The fork distributes a binary bundle containing the component, and the changed terms prohibit that distribution; the provided policy requires a maintainer decision.
The adapter copies seconds into a milliseconds-labeled field, so it needs a unit conversion to display correct millisecond durations.
The callback reads summary from its argument, which now becomes a job identifier; it needs to fetch the result separately.
Persistent cache data moves into a directory excluded by the fork backup, requiring the backup procedure to cover the new location.
Every run now requires interactive browser sign-in and rejects environment tokens, conflicting with the unattended job requirement.
The help bundle now requires a network connection while the workshop room is offline, requiring a fork-specific solution or decision.
The panel takes the first result, but alphabetical ordering does not preserve highest-relevance-first display; its ranking handling needs adaptation.
The service now deletes history after twenty-four hours, shorter than the seven-day audit requirement, and the fork stores no local copy.
The bundle manifest and any Component Z grant are absent, so it is unknown whether the new grant requirement affects or is already satisfied by the release.
The version-2 duration unit is absent, so direct numeric copying cannot be assessed for correct millisecond display.
The callback implementation is absent and may already fetch result URLs; the change alone does not establish a need for adaptation.
The shared-store location and backup inclusion rules are absent, so persistent-data coverage cannot be established.
The delegated authentication flow is absent, so whether it supports the unattended job cannot be assessed.
Network availability and endpoint permissions in the deployment environment are absent, so installation compatibility cannot be established.
Ranking policy B is undefined in the supplied context, so its first result cannot be assessed against the highest-relevance requirement.
The audit interval and local-copy behavior are absent, so thirty-day service retention cannot be compared with the obligation to read every job since the preceding run.

The supplied fork context requires exact upstream mirroring and states there are no fork-local product changes; preserving all added release files satisfies the provided obligation without a stated fork-specific adaptation need.
